name: Dell PowerEdge XE AI servers (XE9785/XE9785L, XE9680 class)
vendor: Dell Technologies (GPUs from NVIDIA, AMD, Intel)
region: Worldwide; sold direct through dell.com and via OEM routes
notes: QUOTE-ONLY. Status deliberately 'draft' with confidence 0.6 because I could NOT reach a Dell product or configuration page for these systems: dell.com/en-us/shop and /en-us/products/... both returned generic Dell landing pages to my fetches, and Dell's shop pages block automated extraction. What IS verified is third-party corroboration of the product's existence and content, which is why this record rests on those sources rather than a Dell page: AMD's own Instinct where-to-buy page names Dell PowerEdge XE9785/XE9785L as a featured 6U system 'with AMD Instinct GPUs for demanding artificial intelligence, machine learning and deep learning applications' and links directly to the Dell storefront; Intel's Gaudi page routes Gaudi buyers to dell.com/en-us/lp/intel-xeon. So DELL IS CONFIRMED as a real enterprise channel for AMD Instinct and Intel Gaudi accelerators by the accelerator vendors themselves, which is stronger evidence than a Dell marketing page would be. No price recorded - not because it is unavailable on request but because I did not see one. BASIS: XE-class servers are 6-8U GPU nodes that ship with the accelerators populated; GPUs are configured options, not separable add-in SKUs at this channel. Anyone comparing a Dell XE node against a bare SXM module is comparing different products. VERIFY BEFORE TRUSTING: re-check the Dell storefront directly in a browser session to capture the configuration pricing model and current lead time. EXPORT CONTROLLED (true). Regime: US BIS advanced-computing export controls (the Oct 2023 interim final rule, 88 FR 73458 - source sup-buy-bis-2023-advanced-computing-controls), which put datacenter accelerators under ECCN 3A090/4A090, added the advanced-computing Foreign Direct Product (FDP) rule, and extended Regional Stability (RS) controls to Country Groups D:1, D:4 and D:5. For items destined to Macau or Country Group D:5 the rule applies a PRESUMPTION OF DENIAL; other RS destinations get a presumption of approval. Practical effect: which accelerator you can legally be sold, and which SKU counts as compliant, is set by destination and end user - not by the channel.
